description: A non-interactive triage of a reported production incident (checkout 503s after a release; the fixture's ops/ files hold the deploy log, alerts and the cause's config change) leaves a blameless postmortem at docs/postmortems/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md with the template's sections, a UTC timeline taken from the supplied records, unknowns marked unknown, a root cause with a confidence word, no recovery claim without a rollback and smoke test, proposed action items with no bead created, and no production code changed. Limits: the checks assert structure and a few planted facts, not the quality of the diagnosis; no gh, release-agent or smoke-test-runner is available in the sandbox, so stabilisation (rollback, approval) is not exercised; the git history is the fixture's single commit, so the timeline can only come from the ops/ files. The skill is plain (found by the model, no command), so the with-skill arm loads packages/quality; the baseline arm gets a plain prompt without the plugin's conventions (file location, template sections, blameless rule, bead rule), so the uplift measures those conventions. Claude only: the skill reads a sibling template through skill://, which Pi loading a single SKILL.md may not resolve (unproven).
prompt:
Production incident: customers report checkout failures (503s) since the afternoon release on 2026-11-10, and it is still failing. The on-call notes and records are in ops/ (start with ops/incident-report.md). Triage it and write up the incident.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions, there is no one to approve anything, so make no production change and create no tickets or issues (list proposed follow-up actions in the write-up instead). There is no network and no gh. Change no source code. Save the write-up under docs/postmortems/.
